newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU mulling karnal bunt grain import curbs.
newsitem.headline: EU mulling karnal bunt grain import curbs.

text.p: The European Commission is mulling curbs on imports of grain and seeds from countries affected by the karnal bunt fungus disease, Commission sources told Reuters.
Under the still-informal plan, the EU would only accept seeds coming from areas declared free from the disease.

Grain, mostly wheat, accepted into the EU would have to be certified as grown in a disease-free area or tested for the disease if it was grown in an area where the fungus was known to occur, they said.
The EU notified the World Trade Organisation (WTO) of its plan in mid-September, the sources said.
WTO members have until November 11 to respond and possibly oppose the plan.
If the plans goes unchallenged, the Commission will seek the opinion of a group of EU phytosanitary experts due to meet on November 18 before making a formal proposal.

The fungus, also called Stinking Smut as it makes flour smell bad, affects grain yield and quality. It affects mostly wheat and durum wheat produced in a limited group of countries including the United States and Mexico.
It was discovered last March in parts of California, Arizona, Texas and New Mexico.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture began a nationwide survey for karnal bunt last Summer.
It announced last Friday that the results of the survey so far showed the U.S. wheat belt was free of the fungus.

On Thursday state agricuture officials said a wheat sample taken from a farm bin in Giles Country, Tennessee, tested positive to the fungus and samples from seven other countries were believed to be positive.
The news triggered fears karnal bunt might surface in other growing areas and pushed wheat futures prices down.
U.S. farm officials have said the latest discovery of the fungus in U.S wheat should have little or no impact on exports. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
